status: PROPOSAL. Nothing here has been checked against the venue, the rental house's datasheets or a load calculation.

provenance.fixtureList: The rental house's list as passed to Claude by the owner on 2026-09-27 (18x UP-B380F, 12x UP-250BSW, 8x UP-HK1915, 50x UP-PL5403, 2x UP-LA40WF, CO2 x6, cold spark x4, smoke x4). The codes are the rental house's internal names, not maker models.
provenance.optics: From the fixtures manifest (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json): each class names a fixture kind whose beam angle and output come from the maker's published page or, where the maker publishes none, a named equivalent — every number carries its source there. The rental house's own datasheets are still OWED to confirm.
provenance.positions: Placed by rule against the hall's structural grid (scripts/place/hall.py -> hall.json), so they move when the hall is rebuilt with measured dimensions.
provenance.hall: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-28.json (flat space-frame roof, 4 spans x 24 m, 18 bays; photos + 2020 satellite) + moxir-hall-features-2026-09-28.json (the owner's zones marked 2026-09-28, the press massing, gates, cranes; sizes estimated).
provenance.models: Fixture bodies are the models in scripts/place/fixtures/glb, built to the datasheet dimensions by scripts/place/fixtures/build_fixtures.py (see the manifest for provenance and licence).
provenance.stage: The owner marked the zones on three photographs on 2026-09-28 ('red backstage, green stage, blue dance floor'); located in metres by a perspective fit of photo 032 (features file, zones._how).

assumptions: The stage stands in the zone the owner marked (green, 2026-09-28): across the nave, its front edge at the white bulk bags, facing the entry and the crane end; the big forging press stands behind it as the backdrop, the backstage (red) behind the press. The audience stands between the crane end and the stage (blue). Positions are estimated from photographs (+-8% of the distance from the crane).

The deck is 16 m wide, 12 m deep, 1.2 m high, its front edge on the zone's front edge; the zone runs on 5.3 m further upstage to the press (backline / crew floor). Deck size is a guess — no stage is on the rental list.

The stage truss is a ground-supported goalpost (two towers standing on the floor either side of the stage + a header) 18 m wide with its header at 6 m, 4 m in from the back of the stage. A guess at a common rental size; no truss is on the list — it is OWED.

UP-PL5403 x50 is read as 50 in total: 32 on the nave columns around the dance floor and the stage (one on each column's nave face, one on its back face, grid lines s 6-48 m), 12 on the next rows out (one span either side, s 12-42 m) so the room reads deep, and 6 on the floor in front of the press, lighting it as the backdrop. The v2 proposal's 8 on the crane bridge are dropped: the crane now parks over the back of the dance floor.

Lasers hang at the top of the truss towers (6 m) and are aimed UP into the roof over the audience; the rig script refuses any laser aim that descends, and any that passes under 3 m above the floor. This is a picture of intent, not a laser safety assessment — a qualified laser safety officer and the national rules (e.g. the Maximum Permissible Exposure limits of IEC 60825-1) are OWED before any 40 W laser is switched on in front of people.
CO2 jets, cold spark and smoke machines are drawn as the machines (their models), standing where they stand; what they emit is not simulated.

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

bsw250.class: 250 W beam/spot/wash hybrid moving head, used here in spot
bsw250.angleNote: used in its spot mode at 15 deg (its zoom is 10-30); candela scaled from the equivalent's 13 deg figure by flux conservation

beeEye.class: 19 x 15 W RGBW bee-eye (K-series style) moving head
beeEye.angleNote: zoom at its tightest, 4 deg, as bee-eyes are used for beam effects

par.angleNote: the UP-PL5403's standard 15 deg lens (source D); candela scaled from the equivalent's 25 deg figure

laser.angleNote: drawn as the narrowest cone di.iiii renders (its cone clamps at 0.57 deg half-angle); a real laser beam is millimetres wide and scanned into shapes, which is not represented
laser.intensityNote: no candela for a laser; it is never one of the real lamps (budget), so this is only the entity's value

groups.note: 8 beams on the stage back line, fanned up into the trusses over the dance floor
10 beams on the floor at the column bases along the dance-floor bays (5 grid lines, both sides), aimed up into the roof
12 on the stage truss header, alternately onto the stage floor and the back wall
8 bee-eyes on the stage floor at the front edge, aimed out and up over the audience
one on each nave column's inner face and one on its back face, grid lines around the dance floor and the stage; the beam-only ones' light is BAKED (wash-glb.mjs)
12 on the next column rows out (one span either side, facing the nave), so the room reads deep; light baked
6 on the floor 3 m in front of the press and the machine line beside it, washing them as the stage's backdrop; the press is off the axis, so this group is not mirrored
2 lasers at the top of the truss towers, aimed up into the roof — never into the audience plane

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.

night.note: A dim, cool night: the hall stays readable so the rig can be judged against it. Tuned by eye in the browser on the RTX 3080 (2026-09-28: ambient 0.35 -> 0.8, directional 0.25 -> 0.35, fog 30/150 -> 60/250 m, because in the 108 m hall the old fog blacked out everything past 30 m and the owner found the room dark). Not a photometric night.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).

roof-cathedral.title: Roof cathedral
roof-cathedral.intent: The hall's own architecture lit as a nave: every column-base beam rises straight up into the trusses in mirrored pairs, a slight lean in toward the centre line; the stage beams open as an apse fan into the lantern; bee-eyes lift low over the house.

fan-out.title: Fan out
fan-out.intent: The stage beams open in one symmetric fan over the house; the column rows lean back toward the stage so every beam in the room reads from the band outward; bee-eyes fan wide and low.

crossfire.title: Crossfire
crossfire.intent: The two column rows fire across the dance floor at each other and cross over its centre line at about 5 m; the stage beams X-cross above the front of the house.

all-to-centre.title: All to centre
all-to-centre.intent: Every beam in the room meets at one point 9 m above the middle of the crowd, 16 m out from the stage — the 'ballyhoo' focus.

curtain.title: Curtain
curtain.intent: A wall of light at the stage line: the stage beams and the bee-eyes stand straight up in two parallel rows and the truss spots drop straight down between them; the column rows lean back to the stage.
